beats.intro: Temperatures drop below zero. Bank balances go negative. Divers go below sea level. [[q]]In this chapter, you'll learn to add numbers that can be positive or negative.
beats.signs: Positive numbers are greater than zero. [[plus]]You can write them with or without a plus sign: plus two and two are the same number. [[neg]]Negative numbers are less than zero, and they always have a minus sign, like negative six.
beats.lineRule: To add on a number line, start at zero. [[pos]]A positive number moves you to the right. [[neg]]A negative number moves you to the left. [[end]]Wherever you stop is the sum.
beats.ex1: Let's add five and negative three. [[m1]]Start at zero and move five to the right. [[m2]]Then move three to the left. [[land]]You stop at two. So five plus negative three is two.
beats.ex2: Now negative one plus negative four. [[m1]]Move one to the left. [[m2]]Then four more to the left. [[land]]You stop at negative five.
beats.ex3: What about five plus negative seven? [[m1]]Move five to the right. [[m2]]Then seven to the left. [[cross]]This time you pass zero. [[land]]You stop at negative two.
beats.q1: Quick check. Use the number line.
beats.opposites: Two numbers the same distance from zero, on opposite sides, are called opposites. [[ex]]Eight and negative eight are opposites. [[m1]]Move eight to the right, [[m2]]then eight to the left, [[land]]and you are back at zero. [[rule]]A number plus its opposite is always zero.
beats.tiles: Here's another way to see it. [[show]]Think of each positive one as a plus tile, and each negative one as a minus tile. [[pair]]A plus tile and a minus tile make zero, so they cancel out. [[ex]]For five plus negative three, lay out five plus tiles and three minus tiles. [[cancel]]Three pairs cancel. [[left]]Two plus tiles are left, so the sum is two.
beats.absValue: One more idea before the shortcut rules. [[dist]]The absolute value of a number is its distance from zero. [[bars]]We write it with two bars. [[ex1]]Negative six is six units from zero, so its absolute value is six. [[ex2]]Six is also six units from zero. [[never]]A distance is never negative, so an absolute value is never negative.
beats.sameSign: Now the shortcuts. [[rule]]When both numbers have the same sign, they move the same way. [[do]]Add their absolute values, and keep the sign they share. [[ex]]Negative six plus negative eight: [[tiles]]six minus tiles and eight minus tiles, with nothing to cancel. [[ans]]Six plus eight is fourteen, and the sign stays negative: negative fourteen.
beats.diffSign: When the signs are different, the numbers pull in opposite directions. [[do]]Subtract the smaller absolute value from the larger one. [[sign]]The answer takes the sign of the number that is farther from zero. [[ex]]Negative eleven plus five: [[tiles]]five pairs cancel, [[left]]and six minus tiles are left. [[calc]]Eleven minus five is six, and negative eleven is farther from zero, so the answer is negative six.
beats.q2: Quick check. Two questions about different signs.
beats.story: An elevator starts at the ground floor, which we call zero. [[up5]]It goes up five floors, [[up2]]then up two more. [[down]]Then it goes down eleven floors to the parking garage. [[q]]Where does it stop? [[expr]]Write each move as a number: plus five, plus two, and negative eleven. [[s1]]Five plus two is seven. [[s2]]Seven plus negative eleven is negative four. [[ans]]The elevator stops four floors below the ground floor.
beats.q3: Quick check. A question about temperature.
beats.wrap: To add positive and negative numbers: [[w1]]if the signs are the same, add the absolute values and keep the sign. [[w2]]If the signs are different, subtract the absolute values, and use the sign of the number farther from zero. [[w3]]A number plus its opposite is zero. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final2: Next, decide whether each sum is positive, negative, or zero, without working it out fully.
beats.final3: Last one. Decide whether each statement is true or false.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter four, adding positive and negative numbers.
